gates.detail: Example sentence capitals/punctuation and contains the word.

issues: The simple meaning covers only the cloth sense. 'Material' more generally means any substance things are made from, such as wood, plastic or metal, so children may form an incomplete idea of the word.
The word family lists only the plural 'materials', which is an inflection rather than a true word-family member, so it adds little learning value.
The applicable grades G3–G4 may not fully cover the ages 8–10 band, which often includes G5.
suggested_fixes: Add a note to the explanation, for example: 'Material can also mean what anything is made of, like wood or plastic.'
Keep 'materials', or add a simple related form if suitable (such as 'raw material' as a collocation) rather than relying on the plural alone.
